basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 31.' and it opens '(Cap. XLVII.—Vers. 31.) Et dixit ei, jura mihi. Et juravit ei: et adoravit Israel contra'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XLVII.—Vers. 31.) Et dixit ei, jura mihi. Et juravit ei: et adoravit Israel contra summitatem virgae ejus. Et in hoc loco quidam frustra simulant adorasse Jacob summitatem sceptri Joseph, quod videlicet honorans filium, potestatem ejus adoraverit, cum in Hebraeo multo aliter legatur: Et adoravit, inquit, Israel ad caput lectuli: quod scilicet, postquam ei juraverat filius securus de petitione, quam rogaverat, adoraverit Deum contra caput lectuli sui. Sanctus quippe, et Deo deditus vir, oppressus senectute, sic habebat lectulum positum, ut ipse jacentis habitus absque ulla difficultate ad orationem esset paratus.
